summary.headline: Ujjivan SFB posted record quarterly PAT of INR365 crores (ROA 2.4%, ROE 19.7%) in Q2 FY27, with deposits up 29.2% to INR50,643 crores.
summary.overview: Ujjivan SFB reported strong Q2 FY27 growth: gross loans rose 32.1% YoY to INR45,699 crores and NII rose 35% YoY to INR1,244 crores, with NIM at 8.4%. Asset quality was stable, with GNPA at 2.1%, NNPA at 0.3%, and a credit cost of 0.7%. Management guided NIM down about 10 bps to around 8.35% in H2 after the 25 bps repo hike, and flagged that ROA could overshoot the guided range. The MD's early retirement is pending a successor, and a preferential equity raise of INR409 crores is subject to shareholder approval.

segments.name: Micro banking (unsecured)
segments.commentary: Book INR22,037 crores, grew about 6% in H1 FY27; FY27 guidance of 12-14% reiterated. Bucket X collection efficiency 99.7%; about 2 lakh customers added in Q2.

segments.name: Affordable housing
segments.commentary: Book INR10,056 crores, crossed INR10,000 crores; GNPA 1.2%, PAR 3.7%; ticket size about INR17.9 lakh; growth about 37-38% on OSP.

segments.name: Micro mortgage
segments.commentary: Book INR2,031 crores, up 85.7% YoY; GNPA 0.7%; PAR around 1.8%, expected to settle at 2.5% to just below 3%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Book INR3,871 crores, up 51.3% YoY; new book above INR3,000 crores with GNPA 0.5%. Operates in top 50 cities, South the largest region.

segments.name: Gold loan
segments.commentary: Book INR1,275 crores, up 209.8% YoY; 117 branches added in H1, similar number planned for H2; disbursement LTV below 78%.

segments.name: Agri banking and 2-wheeler
segments.commentary: Agri book INR914 crores (+79.2% YoY); 2-wheeler loans INR1,081 crores (+64.8% YoY).

segments.name: Insurance / TPP
segments.commentary: Insurance income about INR90 crores in H1; about 50% from credit life. TPP grew 41% QoQ and 30% YoY. IRDAI commission norms are a draft; submissions due October 25.

guidance_outlook: NIM expected to fall about 10 bps to around 8.35% in H2 FY27, from the 25 bps repo hike, partly offset by planned DA changes.
Opex to ATA ratio now seen at about 6.2% versus earlier 6.4% guidance; part of brand spend spills into Q3.
Credit cost in H2 expected in line with H1 (about 0.8%), within the 90-100 bps guided range per the company's stated range; management said H2 run rate equals H1.
ROA could overshoot the upper end of the guided range; management said a significant beat looks highly probable.
Microfinance growth guided at 12-14% for FY27; affordable housing growth about 35% in plan.
Secured share of book at 52% targeted to reach 56% by end FY27, rising about 5% each year.
Balance of up to INR2,000 crore fundraise to be raised before resolution expires in July 2027; INR409 crores preferential issue to IFC, Bajaj Life, HDFC Life and Aditya Birla Sun Life.
CASA ratio expected to be about 2 percentage points below the 30% level by year end, per Hitendra Jha.
capex_capacity: Added 104 branches and 1,335 employees in H1 FY27.
Gold loan branches: 117 added in H1, similar number planned for H2.
Brand campaign launched September 2026 with new ambassador R. Madhavan; spend to reflect in H2 with spillover into Q3.
Digital and technology institution-building spends to reflect in H2 at a slower pace than planned.
Securitization pool increased by INR500 crores in October 2026; described as NIM accretive and P&L neutral.
demand_pricing: Micro banking new customer acquisition rose sequentially with about 2 lakh customers added in Q2; NTB up 34% YoY.
Karnataka book INR2,400 crores, of which only INR15.1 crores is eligible under SLBC drought norms; Maharashtra MFI book INR1,682 crores, with SLBC-eligible agri loans of only INR18 crores.
Management said drought-related government intervention is not yet affecting collections; September collections were about 99.7%.
Individual loan ticket size around INR1.5 lakh is the comfort level; micro mortgage ticket size rising to about INR7.5-7.8 lakh, targeted to stabilize near INR8 lakh.
Deposit growth led by HNI, NR, corporate salary segments and top 80 and top 30 cities, where CASA growth is about 40%.
MDR on UPI payments deferred until after Diwali; if implemented, management expects income upside with no added expense.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins move in H2 FY27 and FY28 given the steeper rate cycle and the secured mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said NIM would fall to about 8.35% in H2 from 8.45% in Q2, with a 10 bps impact from the 25 bps repo hike; mix impact offset by planned DA changes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the drought in Karnataka and Maharashtra on collections and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said credit cost lags by about 6 months and will stay within the guided range. Agri and allied exposure is limited, and Bucket X collection efficiency is 99.7%; microfinance guidance of 12-14% is intact.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the opex budget of about INR250 crores will be spent this year, and is extra provisioning planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex to ATA now seen at about 6.2% versus 6.4% earlier. Siddharth Bharadwaj said H2 credit cost run rate matches H1, with no increase planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for CASA and deposit mobilization?
qa_highlights.answer: Hitendra Jha said CASA growth moderated due to some temporary outflows and that NTB rose 34% YoY. The company will make calibrated SA and retail TD rate revisions; CASA is expected to be about 2 percentage points below 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise full-year ROA guidance upward?
qa_highlights.answer: Siddharth Bharadwaj said a significant beat on the upper end of ROA guidance looks highly probable, citing opex at 6.2% of ATA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the balance equity raise and the MD succession?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the balance of the INR2,000 crore approval will be raised before the resolution expires in July 2027. The NRC aims to complete the MD search in 3 to 4 months from September 1.

risks_watch: Interim CEO status: MD Sanjeev Nautiyal retired early for health reasons; successor search targeted to finish in 3-4 months from September 1.
IRDAI draft on insurance commissions (about 50% of insurance income is credit-life linked); final guidelines and submissions due October 25 are pending.
Drought in Karnataka and Maharashtra, and the broader monsoon risk; PAR trend in group and micro mortgage books inching up.
Repo hike pass-through to cost of funds; management guided to upward cost of funds from Q3.
Borrowings: about INR800 crores repaid in Q2; end-FY borrowing share not disclosed, with a follow-up promised.
Balance of fundraise (about INR1,591 crores of the INR2,000 crore approval) still to be raised before July 2027.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and profitability, with a clear view that ROA will likely beat guidance. Cautious on rates, drought exposure and insurance regulation, and noncommittal on the borrowings mix and MD timing.
key_quotes: This quarter marked an important milestone as we crossed INR50,000 crores in deposits.
So overall, the impact will be restricted to 10 bps, which will be resulting in a NIM of 8.35%.
So it looks like a high probability of a significant beat on the upper end at our ROA.

adds.what: 104 branches added in H1 FY27 (Ujjivan SFB network)
117 gold loan branches added in H1 FY27, similar number planned for H2

growth.why: Management guides FY27 ROA above the 1.8-2% range and opex/ATA down to 6.2%, with microfinance growth guided at 12-14% even though H1 growth was only about 6.5%; the MFI guide is not backed by orders or capacity, while gold loan and branch expansion (117 + similar in H2) give partial backing.

mgmt.note: MD's early retirement is pending a successor; no stated growth plan from a new leader yet.
